Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 8, verses 53–55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they denied the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed Allah is Strong, severe in punishment.﴾ ﴿That is because Allah never changes a favour He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves; and indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins, and We drowned the people of Pharaoh; and they were all wrongdoers.﴾

In the verse there are issues:

The first issue: When He, exalted is He, had explained what He sent down upon the disbelievers of the people of Badr, both in this world and in the next, as we have explained, He followed it by showing that this is His way and custom regarding all of them. So He said: ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾. The meaning: the habit of these people in their disbelief is like the habit of the people of Pharaoh in their disbelief, so these were requited with killing and captivity just as those were requited with drowning. The root of da'b (habit, persistent practice) in the language is the continuation of an action; it is said: "So-and-so yada'bu in such-and-such," meaning he persists in it, is constant in it, and wearies himself. Then custom was called da'b, because a person persists in his custom and is constant in it.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed Allah is Strong, severe in punishment﴾, and the purpose of it is to alert that they have a punishment stored up apart from the immediate punishment that befell them. Then He mentioned what functions as a cause for the punishment He sent down upon them, saying: ﴿That is because Allah never changes a favour He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves﴾. And in it there are issues:

The first issue: His saying: ﴿lam yak﴾ (He never was). Most grammarians say: the nun was only elided because it did not resemble a pure nasal sound, so it resembled the letters of extension and fell at the end, so it was elided by analogy with them, as you say: lam yad'u, lam yarmi, lam yali. Al-Wahidi said: this is refuted by their saying: lam yazin and lam yakhun, where the elision of the nun is not heard here.

Ali ibn Isa answered this, saying: kana and yakunu are the "mother of verbs," because every verb has in it the meaning of kana: when we say "daraba" (he struck), its meaning is "kana darb" (there was a striking), and "yadribu" means "yakunu darb" (there is a striking), and likewise the matter is in all of them. Thus it is established that this word is the mother of verbs, so it is needed to be used in most circumstances, and therefore it admitted this elision, unlike our saying lam yakhun and lam yazin, for there is no need to mention them often, so the difference is evident. And Allah knows best.

The second issue: The Qadi said: the meaning of the verse is that He, exalted is He, bestowed upon them reason, power, removal of obstacles, and facilitation of paths, and the intent is that they should occupy themselves with worship and gratitude and turn away from disbelief. So when they turned these circumstances toward immorality and disbelief, they changed Allah's favour upon themselves, and therefore they deserved the replacement of favours with retributions and of bounties with trials. He said: This is among the most emphatic things that indicate that He, exalted is He, does not begin anyone with punishment or harm, and what He does is only as recompense for past disobedience. And if He, exalted is He, had created them and created their bodies and their intellects initially for the Fire, as those people say, that would not be valid.

Our companions said: the apparent meaning of the verse suggests what the Qadi, the Imam, said, but if we took it upon that, it would follow that the attribute of Allah, exalted is He, is causally dependent upon the act of the human being. That is because Allah's judgment of that change and His will concerning it occur only when the human being performs that act; so if it did not occur at that act, Allah would not have that judgment and that will. Then the act of the human being would be affecting the occurrence of an attribute in the essence of Allah, exalted is He, and the human being would be changing the attribute of Allah and affecting it, and that is impossible by the self-evident intellect. Thus it is established that it is not possible to take this statement in its apparent sense; rather the truth is that the attribute of Allah dominates the attributes of created things, so were it not for His judgment and decree first, it would not be possible for the servant to bring about any of the acts or sayings.

The third issue: He, exalted is He, mentioned again His saying: ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾, and they have mentioned many aspects concerning it:

The first: the second statement serves as an elaboration of the first statement, because the first statement mentions their being seized, and the second mentions their drowning, and that is an elaboration.

The second: that by the first is meant the punishment that befell them at the time of death, and by the second what will befall them in the grave in the Hereafter.

The third: the first statement is His saying: ﴿they denied the signs of Allah﴾, and the second statement is His saying: ﴿they denied the signs of their Lord﴾. The first points to their denial of the divine proofs, and the second points to the fact that He, glory be to Him, nurtured them and bestowed upon them many kinds of favour, yet they denied the proofs of nurture and kindness despite their abundance and their succession upon them. So the necessary effect of the first was seizure, and the necessary effect of the second was destruction and drowning. This shows that ingratitude for favour has a great effect in bringing about ruin and perdition. Then He concluded the statement with His saying: ﴿and they were all wrongdoers﴾, and what is meant by it is that they were wrongdoers to themselves through disbelief and disobedience, and wrongdoers to the rest of people through harm and alienation, and that Allah, exalted is He, destroyed them only because of their wrongdoing. And I say in this context: O Allah, destroy the wrongdoers and purify the face of the earth of them, for their trial has grown great and their evil has multiplied, and no one can repel them except You. So repel them, O Subduer, O Compeller, O Avenger.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 8, verses 53–55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they denied the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed Allah is Strong, severe in punishment.﴾ ﴿That is because Allah never changes a favour He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves; and indeed Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.﴾ ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh and those before them: they denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins, and We drowned the people of Pharaoh; and they were all wrongdoers.﴾

In the verse there are issues:

The first issue: When He, exalted is He, had explained what He sent down upon the disbelievers of the people of Badr, both in this world and in the next, as we have explained, He followed it by showing that this is His way and custom regarding all of them. So He said: ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾. The meaning: the habit of these people in their disbelief is like the habit of the people of Pharaoh in their disbelief, so these were requited with killing and captivity just as those were requited with drowning. The root of da'b (habit, persistent practice) in the language is the continuation of an action; it is said: "So-and-so yada'bu in such-and-such," meaning he persists in it, is constant in it, and wearies himself. Then custom was called da'b, because a person persists in his custom and is constant in it.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed Allah is Strong, severe in punishment﴾, and the purpose of it is to alert that they have a punishment stored up apart from the immediate punishment that befell them. Then He mentioned what functions as a cause for the punishment He sent down upon them, saying: ﴿That is because Allah never changes a favour He has bestowed upon a people until they change what is in themselves﴾. And in it there are issues:

The first issue: His saying: ﴿lam yak﴾ (He never was). Most grammarians say: the nun was only elided because it did not resemble a pure nasal sound, so it resembled the letters of extension and fell at the end, so it was elided by analogy with them, as you say: lam yad'u, lam yarmi, lam yali. Al-Wahidi said: this is refuted by their saying: lam yazin and lam yakhun, where the elision of the nun is not heard here.

Ali ibn Isa answered this, saying: kana and yakunu are the "mother of verbs," because every verb has in it the meaning of kana: when we say "daraba" (he struck), its meaning is "kana darb" (there was a striking), and "yadribu" means "yakunu darb" (there is a striking), and likewise the matter is in all of them. Thus it is established that this word is the mother of verbs, so it is needed to be used in most circumstances, and therefore it admitted this elision, unlike our saying lam yakhun and lam yazin, for there is no need to mention them often, so the difference is evident. And Allah knows best.

The second issue: The Qadi said: the meaning of the verse is that He, exalted is He, bestowed upon them reason, power, removal of obstacles, and facilitation of paths, and the intent is that they should occupy themselves with worship and gratitude and turn away from disbelief. So when they turned these circumstances toward immorality and disbelief, they changed Allah's favour upon themselves, and therefore they deserved the replacement of favours with retributions and of bounties with trials. He said: This is among the most emphatic things that indicate that He, exalted is He, does not begin anyone with punishment or harm, and what He does is only as recompense for past disobedience. And if He, exalted is He, had created them and created their bodies and their intellects initially for the Fire, as those people say, that would not be valid.

Our companions said: the apparent meaning of the verse suggests what the Qadi, the Imam, said, but if we took it upon that, it would follow that the attribute of Allah, exalted is He, is causally dependent upon the act of the human being. That is because Allah's judgment of that change and His will concerning it occur only when the human being performs that act; so if it did not occur at that act, Allah would not have that judgment and that will. Then the act of the human being would be affecting the occurrence of an attribute in the essence of Allah, exalted is He, and the human being would be changing the attribute of Allah and affecting it, and that is impossible by the self-evident intellect. Thus it is established that it is not possible to take this statement in its apparent sense; rather the truth is that the attribute of Allah dominates the attributes of created things, so were it not for His judgment and decree first, it would not be possible for the servant to bring about any of the acts or sayings.

The third issue: He, exalted is He, mentioned again His saying: ﴿Like the custom of the people of Pharaoh﴾, and they have mentioned many aspects concerning it:

The first: the second statement serves as an elaboration of the first statement, because the first statement mentions their being seized, and the second mentions their drowning, and that is an elaboration.

The second: that by the first is meant the punishment that befell them at the time of death, and by the second what will befall them in the grave in the Hereafter.

The third: the first statement is His saying: ﴿they denied the signs of Allah﴾, and the second statement is His saying: ﴿they denied the signs of their Lord﴾. The first points to their denial of the divine proofs, and the second points to the fact that He, glory be to Him, nurtured them and bestowed upon them many kinds of favour, yet they denied the proofs of nurture and kindness despite their abundance and their succession upon them. So the necessary effect of the first was seizure, and the necessary effect of the second was destruction and drowning. This shows that ingratitude for favour has a great effect in bringing about ruin and perdition. Then He concluded the statement with His saying: ﴿and they were all wrongdoers﴾, and what is meant by it is that they were wrongdoers to themselves through disbelief and disobedience, and wrongdoers to the rest of people through harm and alienation, and that Allah, exalted is He, destroyed them only because of their wrongdoing. And I say in this context: O Allah, destroy the wrongdoers and purify the face of the earth of them, for their trial has grown great and their evil has multiplied, and no one can repel them except You. So repel them, O Subduer, O Compeller, O Avenger.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 8, verse 56:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living beings in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve, and they will not believe﴾ ﴿those with whom you made a treaty, then they break their treaty every time, and they do not fear Allah﴾.

Know that when He, exalted is He, described all the disbelievers with His saying, ﴿and all of them were wrongdoers﴾, He singled out some of them with a distinction in evil and obstinacy, so He said: ﴿Indeed, the worst of living beings in the sight of Allah﴾, that is, in His judgment and knowledge, are those in whom two attributes are found:

Page 146
The first attribute: the disbeliever who persists in his disbelief, insisting upon it, never changing from it at all.
The second attribute: that he constantly breaks the covenant. So His saying, ﴿those with whom you made a treaty﴾, is a substitute (badal) for His saying, ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: those among those who disbelieved with whom you made a treaty, and they are the worst of living beings. His saying, ﴿with whom﴾ (min hum), is for partition (li-l-tab'id), since a treaty is only made with their nobles. His saying, ﴿then they break their treaty every time﴾: the people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: the future tense (al-mustaqbal) was conjoined to the past (al-madi) only to clarify that it is their habit to break the covenant time after time. Ibn Abbas said: they are the Banu Qurayzah, for they broke the covenant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and assisted the polytheists against him with weapons on the Day of Badr. Then they said: "We erred," so he made a treaty with them a second time, and they broke it again on the Day of the Trench (al-Khandaq). His saying, ﴿and they do not fear Allah﴾, its meaning is that the custom of one who returns to reason and firmness is to guard against breaking a covenant, so that people are at ease with his word and trust his speech. Thus Allah, exalted is He, made clear that whoever combines persistent disbelief with breaking the covenant in this manner is the worst of living beings.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on Surah 8, verses 57–58:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So if you overcome them in war, then disperse those behind them, that they may take heed.﴾ ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them [their covenant] on equal terms. Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous.﴾

Know that He, exalted is He, at times guides His Messenger to gentleness and kindness, in many verses. Among them is His saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾ [al-Anbiya: 107]. Among them is His saying: ﴿So pardon them, and ask forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter﴾ [Al 'Imran: 159]. At other times He guides to severity and firmness, as in this verse. That is because, when He mentioned those who break their covenant every time, He clarified how they should be dealt with, so He said: ﴿So if you overcome them in war﴾. Al-Layth said: "We found so-and-so (thaqifna) in such-and-such a place," meaning we seized him and gained victory over him. Al-Tashrid is an expression for scattering together with disorder. It is said: "shareda yashrudu shurudan," and "sharrada tashridan." So the meaning of the verse is: if you gain victory in war over these disbelievers who break the covenant, then do to them something that scatters those behind them. Ata said: "Inflict slaughter upon them until others fear you." It was also said: "Punish them with a punishment that scatters others among those who break covenants." ﴿That they may take heed﴾, that is, that those behind them may remember that punishment, and so it will prevent them from breaking the covenant.

Ibn Mas'ud read ﴿فَشَرِّذْ﴾ with a dhal dotted from above, meaning "fa-farriq" (so disperse), and it seems to be an inversion of "shadhdhir." Abu Haywa read ﴿مِن خَلْفِهِمْ﴾. The meaning is: disperse them with a scattering that involves them from behind, because when one of the two armies defeats the other, the victors run after the defeated. So He commanded the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to scatter them at that time.

As for His saying: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people﴾, it means: from a people with whom you have a covenant, treachery and breaking of the pact, by clear signs. ﴿Then throw back to them﴾, that is, cast the covenant back to them in an open and straightforward manner, by making clear to them the abandonment of the covenant and informing them plainly and openly that you have severed what is between you and them. Do not attack them with war while they assume the covenant still stands, for that would be treachery on your part. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love the treacherous﴾ regarding covenants.

The conclusion regarding this verse is that He commanded him to renounce those who break the covenant in the most honorable way, and commanded him to keep as far as possible from everything that gives the impression of breaking and violating the covenant. The scholars said: the signs of breaking a covenant, when they appear, either appear as a probable appearance or as a certain appearance. If it is the first, notifying them is obligatory, as mentioned in this verse. That is because Qurayza had made a covenant with the Prophet (ﷺ), then they responded to Abu Sufyan and those with him of the polytheists, to support them against the Messenger of Allah. So the Messenger of Allah feared treachery from them against him and his companions. In such a case, the leader is obligated to throw back their covenants to them on equal terms and to inform them of war. As for when the breaking of the covenant appears as a certain appearance, then there is no need to renounce the covenant, as the Messenger of Allah did with the people of Makkah. When they broke the covenant by killing Khuza'a, who were under the protection of the Prophet (ﷺ), the army of the Messenger of Allah reached them at Marr al-Zahran, which is four farsakh from Makkah. And Allah, exalted is He, knows best what is correct, and to Him is the return and the final destination.

**Verse:** ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that they have outstripped [Us]. Indeed, they cannot escape.﴾

There are several issues in this verse.

**First issue:** God, may He be exalted, when He explained what the Messenger should do regarding those whom he finds in war and is able to overpower, and also mentioned what must be done with those who openly broke the covenant, then explained the situation of those who escaped him on the day of Badr and elsewhere, so that no regret would remain in his heart. Among them were some who had gone to great lengths in harming the Messenger, peace be upon him. So He said: ﴿And let not those who disbelieve think that they have outstripped﴾. The meaning is: since they have escaped, they have eluded you, and you were not able to inflict upon them what they deserve. There are then two opinions:

The first: the intended meaning is, "Do not think that they have slipped away from you, for God will grant you victory over their caravan."

The second: "Do not think that, because they have been freed from captivity and killing, they have been freed from the punishment of God and from the torment of the Hereafter." ﴿Indeed, they cannot escape﴾, that is, by this outstripping they cannot prevent God from taking vengeance upon them. The purpose is to console the Messenger regarding those who escaped him and whom he was unable to avenge or satisfy himself against.

**Second issue:** Ibn 'Amir and Hafs, on the authority of 'Asim, read ﴿لا يَحْسَبَنَّ﴾ with a yā' with a dot below (i.e., *yaḥsabanna*, third person). There are three ways to justify this:

The first: al-Zajjaj said: "*Wa-lā yaḥsabanna alladhīna kafarū annahum yasbiqūnā*" (and let not those who disbelieve think that they will outstrip us), because in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is *annahum sabaqūnā* (that they outstripped us). If that is the case, then it is like your saying: *ḥasibtu an aqūma* (I thought that I would stand) and *ḥasibtu aqūmu* (I thought I stand). The omission of *an* is frequent in the Qur'an. God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Say: Is it other than God that you order me to worship?﴾ [Az-Zumar: 64], meaning: *an a'bud* (that I worship).

The second: we posit an implied subject for *al-ḥusbān* (the thinking), and make *alladhīna kafarū* the first object, the estimation being: "And let no one think those who disbelieve [...]."

The third: Abu 'Ali said: It is also permissible that the first object be implied, the estimation being: "And let not those who disbelieve think themselves to have outstripped," or "to have outstripped them." As for most of the reciters, they read ﴿ولا تَحْسَبَنَّ﴾ with a tā' with a dot above, addressing the Prophet ﷺ, with *alladhīna kafarū* as the first object, and *sabaqū* as the second object, its place being in the accusative. The meaning is: "And do not think that those who disbelieve are outstripping [you]."

**Third issue:** Most reciters pronounce *inna* with a kasra in His words ﴿إنَّهم لا يُعْجِزُونَ﴾ (indeed they cannot escape), and this is the correct form, because it is the beginning of a new statement not connected to the first, like His words: ﴿Or do those who commit evil deeds think that they can outstrip Us?﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 4]. The statement is complete, and then He says: ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾. Just as His words ﴿Evil is what they judge﴾ are separate from the sentence before them, so also His words ﴿indeed they cannot escape﴾ are separate. Ibn 'Amir read *annahum* with an open alif (*anna*), and made it dependent on the first sentence. There are two aspects to this:

The first: the estimation is: "Do not think them to have outstripped, because they will not escape; so they will be recompensed for their disbelief."

The second: Abu 'Ubayd said: one makes *lā* (not) superfluous (*ṣila*), and the estimation is: "Do not think that they cannot escape."

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 8, verse 60:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And prepare against them whatever you can of strength and of horses stationed at the frontier (ribat al-khayl), by which you may terrify the enemy of God and your enemy, and others besides them whom you do not know, but God knows them. And whatever you spend in the way of God will be repaid to you in full, and you will not be wronged.﴾

Know that when the Most High had made it obligatory for His Messenger to disperse those who had broken the covenant, and to renounce the treaty with those from whom treachery was feared, He commanded him in this verse to prepare against these disbelievers. It has been said that when the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ, in the matter of Badr, set out against the disbelievers without equipment or preparation, God commanded them not to return to the like of that, and to prepare for the disbelievers whatever they could of equipment, preparation and strength. By "strength" is meant here that which is a means to acquiring strength, and they have mentioned several interpretations of it:

The first: what is meant by strength is kinds of weapons.

The second: it is related that the Prophet ﷺ recited this verse from the pulpit and said: "Verily, strength is archery," and he said it three times.

The third: some have said that strength is fortresses.

The fourth: the scholars of meanings (ashab al-ma'ani) said: the better view is that this is general for everything by which one may gain strength in fighting the enemy, and everything that is an instrument of raiding and striving (jihad) is part of strength. The saying of the Prophet ﷺ, "Strength is archery," does not negate the consideration of other things, just as his saying ﷺ, "The Hajj is Arafat," and "Regret is repentance," do not negate the consideration of other things, but indicate that the thing mentioned is a noble part of the intended meaning. The same applies here. This verse indicates that preparing for jihad with arrows, weapons, teaching horsemanship and archery is an obligation, though it is of the obligations of sufficiency (fard al-kifaya, a communal obligation that is discharged when enough people perform it).

As for His words, ﴿and horses stationed at the frontier﴾: ribat means garrisoning, or it is the plural of rabit, as fisal is the plural of fasil. There is no doubt that keeping horses tethered is among the strongest instruments of jihad. It is related that a man said to Ibn Sirin: "So-and-so bequeathed a third of his property for fortresses." Ibn Sirin said: "It should be spent on horses, which are tethered in the way of God and ridden for raiding." The man said: "He only bequeathed it for fortresses." He said: "They are horses. Have you not heard the words of the poet:

"Though I have known, in avoiding death, that the fortresses are horses, not the clay of the villages."

Ikrimah said: "By the stationed horses is meant the females." This is also the view of al-Farra'. The reasoning of this view is that the Arabs call horses, when they are tethered in courtyards and fed in fixed places, rubut (sing. rabit), and rubut is pluralized as ribat, which is a plural of a plural. So the meaning of ribat here is the horses tethered in the way of God. It was interpreted as females because they are the most suitable to be tethered, for their breeding and for the growth of their offspring, so keeping them tethered is more fitting than keeping the stallions. This is what al-Wahidi mentioned.

One may say: rather, applying this word to the stallions is better, because the purpose of tethering horses is fighting on them, and there is no doubt that stallions are stronger for charging, retreating and running, so fighting on them is easier. Therefore it is necessary to restrict this word to them. But since there is a conflict between these two interpretations, it is necessary to take the word in its original meaning, namely that it is a tethered horse, whether a stallion or a female.

Then He, the Most High, mentioned the purpose for which He commanded the preparation of these things, saying: ﴿by which you may terrify the enemy of God and your enemy﴾. This is because when the disbelievers know that the Muslims are ready and prepared for jihad, fully equipped with all the weapons and instruments, they fear them. That fear yields many benefits:

First: they do not intend to enter the abode of Islam.

Second: when their fear grows intense, they may of their own accord agree to pay a poll tax (jizya).

Third: it may become a cause for them to embrace faith.

Fourth: they will not help the rest of the disbelievers.

Fifth: this becomes a cause of greater adornment (of strength) in the abode of Islam.

Then the Most High said: ﴿and others besides them whom you do not know, but God knows them﴾. The meaning is that increasing the instruments and tools of jihad terrifies the enemies whom we know to be enemies, and likewise terrifies the enemies whom we do not know to be enemies. There are several views on this:

The first, which is the most correct, is that they are the hypocrites. The meaning is that increasing the means of raiding, just as it makes the disbelievers fear, likewise makes the hypocrites fear.

If it is said: the hypocrites do not fear fighting, so how does what you have mentioned cause terror?

We say: this terror is of two kinds:

The first: when they witness the strength of the Muslims and the abundance of their equipment and instruments, their hope of seeing them defeated is cut off, and this moves them to abandon disbelief in their hearts and inner selves and to become sincere in faith.

The second: the hypocrite's habit is to wait for misfortunes to occur, and to scheme to sow corruption and division among the Muslims. When he sees the Muslims in the utmost strength, he fears them and abandons these blameworthy acts.

The second view on this matter is what Ibn Jurayj related from Sulayman ibn Musa, who said: the intended ones are the disbelieving jinn. It is related that the Prophet ﷺ recited: ﴿and others besides them whom you do not know, but God knows them﴾, and said: "They are the jinn." Then he said: "Verily, Satan does not afflict anyone in a house in which there is a noble horse." Al-Hasan said: "The neighing of a horse terrifies the jinn." This view is problematic, because the increase of the instruments of jihad cannot be understood to have an effect in terrifying the jinn.

The third view: just as the disbeliever is hostile to the Muslim, so too the Muslim may be hostile to the Muslim. So when a man is strong in condition and rich in weapons, just as his enemies among the disbelievers fear him, so too does everyone who is hostile to him fear him, whether Muslim or disbeliever.

Then the Most High said: ﴿And whatever you spend in the way of God﴾, which is general, covering jihad and all other forms of good, ﴿will be repaid to you in full﴾. Ibn Abbas said: "It will be repaid to you, that is, its reward will not be lost in the Hereafter, and God will give its recompense quickly in this world." ﴿And you will not be wronged﴾, that is, you will not be diminished in reward. When Ibn Abbas gave this interpretation, he recited the words of the Most High: ﴿Each of the two gardens brought forth its produce and did not fall short of it in anything﴾ [al-Kahf: 33].

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 8, verses 61–64:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it, and put your trust in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

Know that when He had explained what terrifies the enemy of strength and readiness, He then explained that when they incline (jana'a), i.e., turn toward reconciliation (sulh), the ruling is to accept the reconciliation. Al-Nadr said: "A man inclined (jana'a) toward so-and-so, and inclined to him when he followed him and submitted to him." The meaning is: if they turn toward reconciliation, then you turn toward it too. He made the pronoun feminine in "la-ha" (to it) because he intended by it the sense of the deed and the inclination, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord, after it, is Forgiving, Merciful﴾, meaning after their deed. The author of "al-Kashshaf" said: al-silm (peace) is feminine in the manner of its opposite, which is war (harb). The poet said:

Peace takes from it what you are pleased with,
and war suffices you from its breaths, sips.

Abu Bakr, on the authority of Asim, read *lil-silmi* with a kasra on the sin, while the rest read it with a fatha; both are dialectal variants (lughatan).

Qatadah said: this verse is abrogated (mansukhah) by His saying: ﴿Kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5] and His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah: 29].

Others said: the verse is not abrogated, but it contains the command to make peace when there is benefit in it. If he sees that reconciling with them is beneficial, he may not truncate it to a full year; and if the power lies with the polytheists, it is permissible for the Muslims to make a truce with them for ten years, and it is not permissible to exceed that, following the example of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for he made a truce with the people of Makkah for ten years, then they broke the covenant before the full term had ended.

As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and put your trust in Allah﴾, the meaning is: entrust the matter of what you have agreed with them to Allah, so that He may be a help to you in safety, and so that He may give you victory over them if they break the covenant and turn away from fulfilling it. Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, as an admonition against breaking the peace, because He knows what the servants conceal and hears what they say. Mujahid said: the verse was revealed concerning Qurayzah and al-Nadir, but its application to them does not prevent its being applied to its apparent general meaning. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they intend to deceive you, then indeed Allah is sufficient for you. It is He who strengthened you with His help and with the believers.﴾ ﴿And He joined their hearts together. Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts, but Allah joined them. Indeed, He is All-Mighty, All-Wise.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, had commanded reconciliation in the preceding verse, He mentioned in this verse one of the rulings of reconciliation, which is that if they make peace by way of deception, it is obligatory to accept that peace; for the ruling is built on the outward appearance, since reconciliation cannot be of a higher status than faith. When we base the matter of faith on the outward and not the inward, then here it is more fitting. Therefore He said: ﴿And if they intend﴾, the referent being those mentioned in His saying: ﴿And if they incline to peace﴾.

If it is said: Did He not say: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them [the treaty]﴾ [al-Anfal: 58], i.e., make clear the breaking of that covenant? Does this not contradict what He mentions in this verse?

We say: His saying: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people﴾ is to be understood as applying when that fear is confirmed by strong signs indicating it. This deception is to be understood as applying when there has arisen in their hearts a kind of hypocrisy and falsification, but no signs have appeared indicating that they intend evil and the stirring up of strife; rather, the apparent condition of them was steadfastness in the matter and abstention from dispute. Then, when He mentioned that, He said: ﴿then indeed Allah is sufficient for you﴾, i.e., Allah suffices you, and He is your sufficiency. "This suffices me" and "this is enough for me" are equivalent. ﴿It is He who strengthened you with His help.﴾ The exegetes said: meaning He strengthened and aided you with His help on the day of Badr. I say: this restriction is an error, because the affair of the Prophet (peace be upon him), from the beginning of his life to the end of his death, moment by moment, was a divine affair and a lofty ordinance, in which the acquisition of creatures had no part. Then He said: ﴿and with the believers﴾. Ibn Abbas said: this means the Ansar.

If it is said: When He said: ﴿It is He who strengthened you with His help﴾, what need was there, along with His help, for the believers, so that He said: ﴿and with the believers﴾?

We say: support (ta'yid) comes only from Allah, but it is of two kinds:

The first: what occurs without the intermediary of known and customary causes.

The second: what occurs through the intermediary of known and customary causes.

The first is what is meant by His saying: "strengthened you with His help", and the second is what is meant by His saying: "and with the believers". Then He, exalted is He, explained how He strengthened him with the believers, saying: ﴿Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts, but Allah joined them﴾. In this there are several issues:

First issue: The Prophet (ﷺ) was sent to a people whose pride was intense and whose zeal was great, to the extent that if a man of one tribe was slapped, his tribe would fight on his behalf until they had avenged him. Then they changed from that condition, so that a man fought his brother, his father and his son, and they agreed on obedience and became helpers, and became aides. It is said: they were the Aws and the Khazraj, for the enmity between them had been severe and the warfare constant; then the rancor departed, and familiarity and love arose. The removal of that severe enmity and its replacement with strong love and complete sincerity is something only Allah, exalted is He, is able to do, and this became a manifest miracle attesting to the truthfulness of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Second issue: Our companions (the Ash'aris) argued by this verse that the states of the hearts, including beliefs, volitions and affections, are all created by Allah, exalted is He. For that familiarity, affection and intense love arose only through faith and following the Messenger, upon him be blessings and peace. So if faith were an act of the servant and not an act of Allah, exalted is He, then the love that follows from it would be an act of the servant and not an act of Allah, exalted is He, and that is contrary to the plain meaning of the verse. The Qadi said: were it not for the subtle kindnesses of Allah, exalted is He, moment by moment, these states would not have come about; so that sincerity is attributed to Allah, exalted is He, upon this interpretation. Its parallel is that a child's knowledge and good manners are attributed to his father, because they came about only through the father's assistance and upbringing; so likewise here.

The answer: All that you have mentioned is a departure from the apparent meaning and an carrying of the speech toward metaphor. Moreover, all these subtle kindnesses were present in the case of the disbelievers just as they were present in the case of the believers, so if nothing else had occurred there beyond the subtle kindnesses, there would be no benefit in specifying the believers with these meanings. Furthermore, rational proof strengthens the apparent meaning of this verse, for the heart may become characterized by desire instead of aversion and vice versa, so the preponderance of one of the two sides over the other must have a determinant. If that determinant is the servant, the division returns; and if it is Allah, exalted is He, then that is what is intended. Thus it is known that the plain meaning of this verse is confirmed by plain rational proof, so there is no need for what the Qadi mentioned in this matter.

Third issue: This verse indicates that before they began Islam and following the Messenger, the people were in constant enmity and fierce warfare, one killing another and one raiding another. When they believed in Allah and His Messenger and the Last Day, the disputes ceased, the harshness was removed, and complete affection and intense love arose.

Know that the verification in this matter is that love arises only upon the conception of the attainment of some good and perfection. Love is thus a state caused by that particular conception; whenever this conception is present, love is present, and whenever the conception of evil and hatred arises, aversion is present. Now, goods and perfections are of two kinds:

One: the lasting, enduring goods and perfections, free from aspects of change and alteration; these are the spiritual perfections and the divine felicities.

The second: the changing and altering perfections, which are the bodily perfections and the corporeal felicities, for they are swiftly changing and altering, like mercury that moves from state to state. A person imagines that in the company of Zayd there is great wealth, so he loves him; then it occurs to him that this wealth will not be obtained, so he hates him. For this reason it has been said that the lover and the beloved sometimes experience desire and aversion between them several times in a single day; for the beloved desires the lover for his wealth, and the lover desires the beloved for the sake of bodily pleasure, and these two matters are prone to change and transition. Therefore the love between them and the enmity between them are not lasting, but are swift to vanish and transition.

Having known this, we say: if what necessitates love and affection is the pursuit of worldly goods and corporeal felicities, that love is swift to vanish and transition, because love follows the conception of perfection, and the conception of perfection follows the attainment of that perfection. So when that perfection is swift to vanish and transition, its effects are swift to change and vanish. But if what necessitates love is the conception of lasting, sanctified perfections free from change and vanishing, that love too is lasting and safe from change, because the state of the effect in permanence and change follows the state of the cause. This is what is meant by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67].

Having known this, we say: the Arabs before the coming of the Messenger were seekers of wealth, status and boasting, and their love was caused by this cause; therefore that love was swift to vanish, and with the slightest cause they fell into wars and strife. When the Messenger (ﷺ) came and called them to the worship of Allah, exalted is He, and to turning away from this world and turning toward the Hereafter, the enmity and harshness were removed from them, and they became brothers in agreement. Then after his death, peace be upon him, when the doors of this world were opened for them and they turned to seeking it, they returned to fighting one another and warring with one another. This is the true cause in this matter.

Then He, exalted is He, concluded this verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is All-Mighty, All-Wise﴾, i.e., Almighty, Irresistible, able to dispose of hearts and turn them from enmity to friendship and from aversion to desire. ﴿All-Wise﴾ in doing what He does with perfect firmness and mastery, or conforming to what is beneficial and right, according to the two opinions on compulsion and predestination.

Know that when He, exalted is He, had commanded reconciliation in the preceding verse, He mentioned in this verse one of the rulings of reconciliation, which is that if they make peace by way of deception, it is obligatory to accept that peace; for the ruling is built on the outward appearance, since reconciliation cannot be of a higher status than faith. When we base the matter of faith on the outward and not the inward, then here it is more fitting. Therefore He said: ﴿And if they intend﴾, the referent being those mentioned in His saying: ﴿And if they incline to peace﴾.

If it is said: Did He not say: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people, then throw back to them [the treaty]﴾ [al-Anfal: 58], i.e., make clear the breaking of that covenant? Does this not contradict what He mentions in this verse?

We say: His saying: ﴿And if you fear treachery from a people﴾ is to be understood as applying when that fear is confirmed by strong signs indicating it. This deception is to be understood as applying when there has arisen in their hearts a kind of hypocrisy and falsification, but no signs have appeared indicating that they intend evil and the stirring up of strife; rather, the apparent condition of them was steadfastness in the matter and abstention from dispute. Then, when He mentioned that, He said: ﴿then indeed Allah is sufficient for you﴾, i.e., Allah suffices you, and He is your sufficiency. "This suffices me" and "this is enough for me" are equivalent. ﴿It is He who strengthened you with His help.﴾ The exegetes said: meaning He strengthened and aided you with His help on the day of Badr. I say: this restriction is an error, because the affair of the Prophet (peace be upon him), from the beginning of his life to the end of his death, moment by moment, was a divine affair and a lofty ordinance, in which the acquisition of creatures had no part. Then He said: ﴿and with the believers﴾. Ibn Abbas said: this means the Ansar.

If it is said: When He said: ﴿It is He who strengthened you with His help﴾, what need was there, along with His help, for the believers, so that He said: ﴿and with the believers﴾?

We say: support (ta'yid) comes only from Allah, but it is of two kinds:

The first: what occurs without the intermediary of known and customary causes.

The second: what occurs through the intermediary of known and customary causes.

The first is what is meant by His saying: "strengthened you with His help", and the second is what is meant by His saying: "and with the believers". Then He, exalted is He, explained how He strengthened him with the believers, saying: ﴿Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have joined their hearts, but Allah joined them﴾. In this there are several issues:

First issue: The Prophet (ﷺ) was sent to a people whose pride was intense and whose zeal was great, to the extent that if a man of one tribe was slapped, his tribe would fight on his behalf until they had avenged him. Then they changed from that condition, so that a man fought his brother, his father and his son, and they agreed on obedience and became helpers, and became aides. It is said: they were the Aws and the Khazraj, for the enmity between them had been severe and the warfare constant; then the rancor departed, and familiarity and love arose. The removal of that severe enmity and its replacement with strong love and complete sincerity is something only Allah, exalted is He, is able to do, and this became a manifest miracle attesting to the truthfulness of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Second issue: Our companions (the Ash'aris) argued by this verse that the states of the hearts, including beliefs, volitions and affections, are all created by Allah, exalted is He. For that familiarity, affection and intense love arose only through faith and following the Messenger, upon him be blessings and peace. So if faith were an act of the servant and not an act of Allah, exalted is He, then the love that follows from it would be an act of the servant and not an act of Allah, exalted is He, and that is contrary to the plain meaning of the verse. The Qadi said: were it not for the subtle kindnesses of Allah, exalted is He, moment by moment, these states would not have come about; so that sincerity is attributed to Allah, exalted is He, upon this interpretation. Its parallel is that a child's knowledge and good manners are attributed to his father, because they came about only through the father's assistance and upbringing; so likewise here.

The answer: All that you have mentioned is a departure from the apparent meaning and an carrying of the speech toward metaphor. Moreover, all these subtle kindnesses were present in the case of the disbelievers just as they were present in the case of the believers, so if nothing else had occurred there beyond the subtle kindnesses, there would be no benefit in specifying the believers with these meanings. Furthermore, rational proof strengthens the apparent meaning of this verse, for the heart may become characterized by desire instead of aversion and vice versa, so the preponderance of one of the two sides over the other must have a determinant. If that determinant is the servant, the division returns; and if it is Allah, exalted is He, then that is what is intended. Thus it is known that the plain meaning of this verse is confirmed by plain rational proof, so there is no need for what the Qadi mentioned in this matter.

Third issue: This verse indicates that before they began Islam and following the Messenger, the people were in constant enmity and fierce warfare, one killing another and one raiding another. When they believed in Allah and His Messenger and the Last Day, the disputes ceased, the harshness was removed, and complete affection and intense love arose.

Know that the verification in this matter is that love arises only upon the conception of the attainment of some good and perfection. Love is thus a state caused by that particular conception; whenever this conception is present, love is present, and whenever the conception of evil and hatred arises, aversion is present. Now, goods and perfections are of two kinds:

One: the lasting, enduring goods and perfections, free from aspects of change and alteration; these are the spiritual perfections and the divine felicities.

The second: the changing and altering perfections, which are the bodily perfections and the corporeal felicities, for they are swiftly changing and altering, like mercury that moves from state to state. A person imagines that in the company of Zayd there is great wealth, so he loves him; then it occurs to him that this wealth will not be obtained, so he hates him. For this reason it has been said that the lover and the beloved sometimes experience desire and aversion between them several times in a single day; for the beloved desires the lover for his wealth, and the lover desires the beloved for the sake of bodily pleasure, and these two matters are prone to change and transition. Therefore the love between them and the enmity between them are not lasting, but are swift to vanish and transition.

Having known this, we say: if what necessitates love and affection is the pursuit of worldly goods and corporeal felicities, that love is swift to vanish and transition, because love follows the conception of perfection, and the conception of perfection follows the attainment of that perfection. So when that perfection is swift to vanish and transition, its effects are swift to change and vanish. But if what necessitates love is the conception of lasting, sanctified perfections free from change and vanishing, that love too is lasting and safe from change, because the state of the effect in permanence and change follows the state of the cause. This is what is meant by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67].

Having known this, we say: the Arabs before the coming of the Messenger were seekers of wealth, status and boasting, and their love was caused by this cause; therefore that love was swift to vanish, and with the slightest cause they fell into wars and strife. When the Messenger (ﷺ) came and called them to the worship of Allah, exalted is He, and to turning away from this world and turning toward the Hereafter, the enmity and harshness were removed from them, and they became brothers in agreement. Then after his death, peace be upon him, when the doors of this world were opened for them and they turned to seeking it, they returned to fighting one another and warring with one another. This is the true cause in this matter.

Then He, exalted is He, concluded this verse with His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is All-Mighty, All-Wise﴾, i.e., Almighty, Irresistible, able to dispose of hearts and turn them from enmity to friendship and from aversion to desire. ﴿All-Wise﴾ in doing what He does with perfect firmness and mastery, or conforming to what is beneficial and right, according to the two opinions on compulsion and predestination.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 8, verses 61–64:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if they incline to peace, then incline to it, and put your trust in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.﴾

Know that when He had explained what terrifies the enemy of strength and readiness, He then explained that when they incline (jana'a), i.e., turn toward reconciliation (sulh), the ruling is to accept the reconciliation. Al-Nadr said: "A man inclined (jana'a) toward so-and-so, and inclined to him when he followed him and submitted to him." The meaning is: if they turn toward reconciliation, then you turn toward it too. He made the pronoun feminine in "la-ha" (to it) because he intended by it the sense of the deed and the inclination, as in His saying: ﴿Indeed your Lord, after it, is Forgiving, Merciful﴾, meaning after their deed. The author of "al-Kashshaf" said: al-silm (peace) is feminine in the manner of its opposite, which is war (harb). The poet said:

Peace takes from it what you are pleased with,
and war suffices you from its breaths, sips.

Abu Bakr, on the authority of Asim, read *lil-silmi* with a kasra on the sin, while the rest read it with a fatha; both are dialectal variants (lughatan).

Qatadah said: this verse is abrogated (mansukhah) by His saying: ﴿Kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ [al-Tawbah: 5] and His saying: ﴿Fight those who do not believe in Allah﴾ [al-Tawbah: 29].

Others said: the verse is not abrogated, but it contains the command to make peace when there is benefit in it. If he sees that reconciling with them is beneficial, he may not truncate it to a full year; and if the power lies with the polytheists, it is permissible for the Muslims to make a truce with them for ten years, and it is not permissible to exceed that, following the example of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for he made a truce with the people of Makkah for ten years, then they broke the covenant before the full term had ended.

Therefore He said: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾, as an admonition against breaking the peace, because He knows what the servants conceal and hears what they say. Mujahid said: the verse was revealed concerning Qurayzah and al-Nadir, but its application to them does not prevent its being applied to its apparent general meaning. And Allah knows best.
